gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-adlam-unjoined: Eater is dark and aggressive, its thin strokes softened like letters stamped in soft metal; Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined sits beneath. Eater earns its keep when it is big and short.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-anatolian-hierogl: Wide-set, hairline-free strokes give Eater a dark, aggressive edge, while Noto Sans Anatolian Hieroglyphs points its terminals outward. Let the body text stay modest in size; its tall x-height carries it.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-arabic: Dark, aggressive Eater keeps its thin strokes soft and its letters widely spaced, with only a soft shift in thickness. But Noto Sans Arabic handles the reading, its small letters opened wide.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-armenian: Noto Sans Armenian reads friendly and tall, its round letters wide and inviting. What lingers is the clash, dark aggressive Eater with its widely spaced letters against all that welcoming openness.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-avestan: Eater arrives dark and aggressive, its curves joining stems a little thinner. Noto Sans Avestan is the steadier partner, a modern sans whose open curve tips and tall x-height make the contrast the whole point.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-balinese: Aggressive and dark, Eater spreads wide gaps between its letters. Noto Sans Balinese gives every curve breathing space and keeps its ascenders short, and the clash between them is the draw.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-bamum: Wide, dark and snarling, Eater keeps its strokes lightly modulated, free of any harsh thin spots. Noto Sans Bamum glides line after line, its counters big and open.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-bassa-vah: Dark and aggressive, Eater carries thin strokes of respectable weight; Noto Sans Bassa Vah has a dominant midsection. That mismatch of sturdy and snarling is the real draw here.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-batak: Heavier verticals tugging against lighter horizontals give Eater its dark, aggressive pull. Noto Sans Batak, with a towering x-height and an e that never squeezes shut, keeps text approachable.
gen-eater-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Snarling but restrained: Eater shifts weight only modestly within each stroke, while Noto Sans Bengali keeps capitals barely taller than lowercase. Next to each other, one growls and the other simply talks.
